ue6f51c1a1f: In the shutdown current test, the programmer measures the current consumed by the device in soft shutdown mode while the USB programming interface supplies power to it. As shown in ⟦1⟧Shutdown current test⟦/1⟧, after the device is connected to a USB programming channel of the programmer, the programmer display shows the device's current consumption in real time. If the measured value exceeds the set threshold in several consecutive measurements, the programmer reports an error. If the device's instantaneous current exceeds 160mA, the programmer cuts off power to the USB port and reports an error; the programmer must then be restarted before testing can continue.

ubdb04c54c6: Operation and debugging guide for upgrading devices with batteries attached
uda2aba6486: Purpose and principle of the [Device with battery attached] option
u33dddd4c15: ⟦1⟧With [Device with battery attached] (样机带电池) checked⟦/1⟧: the programmer continuously sends the upgrade command. This ensures that during its brief reset, the device receives the command in time and successfully enters upgrade mode, instead of resetting and running the original application again.
ufd017cbe76: ⟦1⟧With [Device with battery attached] unchecked⟦/1⟧: the programmer takes over power control. The process is: the programmer powers on the device and sends the upgrade command -> if this succeeds, the upgrade starts; if it fails, the programmer cuts the power, then powers on again and retries, repeating this cycle.
u31b073f0b1: ⟦1⟧Note⟦/1⟧: If the device is actually being upgraded with its battery attached but this option is not checked (the USB cable is simply plugged in), there is some chance of entering upgrade mode by resetting with the button, but the recognition rate is extremely low. This is because it is hard to time the reset so that it avoids the programmer's power-on or power-off delay phases. Even if recognition occasionally succeeds, subsequent steps such as frequency offset calibration or chip testing may fail because of power control conflicts. Therefore, ⟦2⟧be sure to check [Device with battery attached] when upgrading with the battery attached⟦/2⟧.
u644b067edb: Key requirement for upgrading with the battery attached
u32c9fed42e: The key to a successful upgrade with the battery attached is that the device must have a "reset process" or an equivalent reset mechanism. There are four common reset methods:
u4a0dc1f57b: ⟦1⟧Hardware switch reset⟦/1⟧: the board has a physical switch that directly disconnects and reconnects the battery to perform a power-on reset (similar to the programmer controlling power-off and power-on).
u741660a035: ⟦1⟧Button reset⟦/1⟧: a long or short press of the reset button (Reset key) on the board triggers a restart and entry into upgrade mode.
u1fac4b6e44: ⟦1⟧Signal/command reset⟦/1⟧: the SDK firmware running on the device supports monitoring level changes on the DP/DM pins of the programmer's USB port, or receiving a specific command sent by the programmer, to trigger a reset.
uf374d67041: ⟦1⟧Voltage-triggered reset⟦/1⟧: the device's SDK uses changes in the programmer's USB_VCC voltage to trigger a reset. In this case, USB_VCC must be set to ON in the deployment screen.
ub9d10a7496: Troubleshooting steps when the reset method is unknown
u9c84c19845: If you are not sure which reset method the current device supports, try the following steps to troubleshoot:
ueec29a7dd0: Check [Device with battery attached] (样机带电池) and plug the device's USB into the programmer.
u3965f8e146: Turn off the programmer's USB_VCC (or switch off the per-port power switch).
ue783008150: Physically disconnect the positive terminal of the device's battery, then reconnect it (simulating a power-on reset).
ue7c28b9d9a: Check whether the programmer recognizes the device and programs it. If nothing happens, repeat the "disconnect-reconnect" operation several times.
ub0907ade17: ⟦1⟧Conclusion⟦/1⟧: If this method cannot enter upgrade mode, it usually means that the device does not support regular upgrades with the battery attached.
uc3d93e1afa: Check whether the device's power supply is connected to the programmer's USB_VCC. If USB_VCC is OFF, it may pull down the device voltage and cause a power supply problem.
ud5d9b50da1: Try leaving [Device with battery attached] unchecked and physically disconnecting the device's battery, and see whether the upgrade works normally.
u30aaa225b6: If the upgrade succeeds with the battery disconnected, the upgrade path between the programmer and the device is working. If you then check [Device with battery attached] again and disconnect and reconnect the battery, the upgrade usually succeeds as well.
u55962d181e: If the "disconnect/reconnect battery" method above works, the upgrade path is fine, and the key is to determine how the device can be triggered to reset while the battery is permanently connected. Consult the device's application developer or hardware circuit designer directly.
ucfb21ff154: ⟦1⟧Try upgrading via the USB private protocol⟦/1⟧:
u14581203d0: If none of the above methods works, try checking [USB-device with battery attached] (usb样机带电池).
u0526b983b4: This method applies when the device is recognized as a USB device (such as an audio device, disk or mouse) when plugged into a PC, and the device has the private protocol enabled and supports receiving the USB upgrade reset command sent by the programmer.
u25cdf37047: If none of the above methods solves the problem, you can use the Forced Upgrade Tool to recognize the device and control the upgrade with the 1-to-1 PC tool.
u855e01da2e: Upgrading crystal-less chips with the battery attached
u47d420ccb5: The key difference between crystal-less chips and chips with a crystal when upgrading with the battery attached lies in ⟦1⟧where the clock system is initialized⟦/1⟧. This directly determines whether the chip can still communicate with the programmer when the firmware is abnormal or the Flash is empty. Details are as follows:
u1efa29103e: For models that support crystal-less upgrades with the battery attached (such as AC632N, AC695X, AC696X and AC608N), clock initialization is usually performed in the ⟦1⟧uboot⟦/1⟧ stage. Therefore, whether an upgrade with the battery attached is possible depends mainly on whether the device's current application supports it.⟦2/⟧ If the ⟦3⟧flash uboot⟦/3⟧ is erased during the upgrade, or the ⟦4⟧flash⟦/4⟧ is empty, the device cannot complete clock initialization after a reset with the battery attached, and therefore cannot establish normal USB or UART communication with the programmer, so the upgrade fails.
uc5156e8769: 2. Upgrade advantages of chips with a crystal
uc98e74f10a: Unlike crystal-less chips, chips with a crystal already have their clock system properly initialized within the ⟦1⟧maskrom⟦/1⟧. This means that even if the chip is blank or its internal firmware is incomplete, as long as it is reset with the battery attached, the chip can still start its low-level communication module normally,⟦2/⟧and thus connect to the programmer and complete the upgrade.
uc8297f0547: Crystal-less upgrades with the battery attached have a lower fault tolerance and depend heavily on the integrity of ⟦1⟧uboot⟦/1⟧; chips with a crystal, thanks to the support of the low-level hardware (⟦2⟧maskrom⟦/2⟧), have more robust communication and do not depend on the flash uboot part. That said, some models also support initializing the clock system in the maskrom when used without a crystal.
u072cbca008: In the normal production process, device frequency offset calibration is performed one device at a time with a test box. To eliminate the separate frequency offset calibration step, the devices' frequency offset is calibrated indirectly through a test box while the 1-to-8 programmer programs the chip firmware in mass production, which improves production efficiency.
uaf64d527be: The test box works in calibration signal transmit mode, continuously transmitting a reference signal as the reference source. After the 1-to-8 programmer has programmed the code into the device's chip, it puts the device into frequency offset calibration mode,
u6bc0408f0e: and the device's chip continuously receives the reference signal sent by the test box, using it as the reference source to calibrate its own frequency offset.
u2d20958441: Device frequency offset calibration calibrates the reference frequency. After the frequency offset calibration, the programmer programs the calibration parameters into a designated storage area of the chip, and the SDK reads them directly for frequency compensation; customers do not need to be concerned with the implementation details.

ua8b834dc13: Devices with a faulty MIC need to be picked out during production so that the MIC can be replaced or the device circuit repaired. How can devices with a faulty MIC be picked out quickly?
ue1b5253e8f: You can use the 1-to-8 programmer to test the MIC on each device while programming the device's chip firmware, and detect devices with a faulty MIC, for example, devices whose MIC picks up no sound.
u44de270f70: If the device's MIC is normal, programming passes; if the MIC is faulty, the programmer reports an error.
u21da602f98: In this way, devices with a faulty MIC can be picked out and kept from passing on to later production stages, which improves production efficiency.
